subject: Results & next tests: Redwood vs HypCloud — regression & hallucination check plan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Results & next tests: Redwood vs HypCloud — regression & hallucination check plan

Hi Priya / Raj,

Thanks again for the demo today — I appreciate the clarity on your latency SLOs and the Regulated Data constraints. As promised, I pulled together a concise next-step plan so we can run an apples-to-apples quality pass vs the HypCloud API you mentioned. High level: we want to validate generation quality on your top 3 flows, measure hallucination rates, and run a small regression sweep on our quantized variant.

Attached: eval_prompts.txt (seed prompts from the demo) and a draft mutual_action_plan.pdf.

Proposed test matrix (quick):
- Flows: release-notes summarization, customer-support triage, policy-extraction
- Metrics: exact-match for key facts, hallucination rate (false fact per 1000 tokens), response latency percentile (p50/p95)
- Models: HypCloud-standard, Redwood-gptx-quant (8-bit), Redwood-gptx-ptq
- Inputs: 250 prompt samples per flow (randomized with seeding)

Immediate asks for Acme:
1) Share the HypCloud sample outputs (or API access) for the same prompt set — Raj, can you share a short export (JSON or CSV)?
2) Confirm any redaction rules we should apply to the prompts/data (PII removal).

Internal owners: Jordan will run the quality eval suite; Ben will own infra and throughput comparisons; Evelyn — looping you for visibility on timeline/SLA asks.

Proposed cadence:
- Jan 9: exchange test vectors and HypCloud output
- Jan 13–16: run evaluation and regression checks
- Jan 18: share consolidated results + recommended rollout plan

If that timeline looks good I’ll schedule the working session with Jordan and Ben.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference
Attachments: eval_prompts.txt (text), mutual_action_plan.pdf (pdf)

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A few quick notes:

- I exported a small HypCloud run for the demo prompts and attached hypcloud-sample-outputs.zip. It contains JSON with HypCloud outputs for the 50 demo prompts; we can extend to the full 250 after we align on redaction.
- Security: our security team requires that you run the prompts with PII redacted; we can provide a redaction regex and a short sanitized dataset if helpful.
- Can you confirm whether your quantized run will preserve exact-match for entity extraction? We need to see trade-offs before committing to a rollout.

We’re available for the Jan 9 handoff — I can grant a short-term API key to mirror the HypCloud results if that eases comparison.

—Raj

Jordan: please review hypcloud-sample-outputs.zip and run the initial 50-prompt comparison. Key things to compute: hallucination per 1000 tokens, entity-extraction exact-match, and p95 latency (from their timestamps). Use the eval_prompts.txt seed mapping attached in the original thread.

Ben: stand up a small isolated job for Redwood-gptx-quant (8-bit) and run on the same 50 prompts; record resource consumption (GPU util, memory) and per-token cost estimate. If the quantized variant diverges >6% on entity exact-match we'll include full PTQ run.
